name: MiddlewarePipeline
purpose: Ordered chain of components that each transform the RequestContext and decide whether to call the next, enabling cross-cutting concerns.
api_signature:
from typing import Awaitable, Callable, Protocol

Next = Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]

class Middleware(Protocol):
    async def __call__(self, ctx: RequestContext, call_next: Next) -> None: ...

class MiddlewarePipeline(Protocol):
    def use(self, mw: Middleware) -> 'MiddlewarePipeline': ...
    async def run(self, ctx: RequestContext) -> None: ...
invariants: Execution order MUST be the registration order; swap or insert operations SHALL be explicit, never implicit.
A middleware that does NOT await call_next MUST short-circuit the remainder of the pipeline.
Each middleware CANNOT bypass downstream error handling: exceptions NEVER skip registered error filters.
Registration MUST be frozen before run() is first called; adding middleware at request time SHALL raise.
MUST produce a response even if every middleware halts; an unhandled halt SHALL yield a 500 by contract.
extension_contract: Consumers add behavior by implementing Middleware and calling pipeline.use(); alternative styles (NestJS interceptor, Plug module, ASP.NET IMiddleware, Rack app) MUST be bound via an adapter that forwards (ctx, call_next) and preserves ordering.
why_essential: Authentication, logging, rate limiting, and error shaping are the same kind of component; without one chain contract, each feature reimplements ordering and every new concern reopens the same debate.
alternatives_considered: AOP via bytecode weaving — invisible and hard to debug
